newsitem.title: USA: Pataki ends pact on Indians' gasoline, cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: Pataki ends pact on Indians' gasoline, cigarette tax.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki Thursday backed away from an attempt to level the playing field between Indian reservations and convenience stores for sales of gasoline and cigarettes.
Pataki said he sent a bill to the legislature that would let stores on Indian reservations sell tax-free gasoline and cigarettes.

Pataki's move would allow stores that had agreed to raise prices for gasoline and cigarettes to now reduce them back to levels charged before their tax-free advantage was challenged by off-reservation convenience stores.
His move stunned the Independent Petroluem Marketers of New York, which had challenged the tax-free advantage of Indian Reservations in a lawsuit.

"I just don't understand why, when you're this close to resolving an issue, you'd walk away like this," said Bob Reid, the group's executive director. He added it had not yet decided whether to takes its fight back to the courts.

In a prepared statement, Pataki said, "These steps will allow the Indian Nations to manage these enterprises on their own, as they have done for decades. Let me make my message to all Indian Nations clear: It is your land, we respect your sovereignty and, if the legislature acts as I am requesting, you will have the right to sell tax-free gasoline and cigarettes free from interference from New York State."

American Indians and the state have battled over the issue for years and in March, Pataki reached interim pacts with six Indian Nations under which five of the tribes agreed to raise cigarette prices as a first step in getting "an acceptable level of parity," while the sixth said it would do the same for gasoline.
The issue led to a violent confrontation several weeks ago at an Indian protest outside Buffalo.
